To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proteome of the rat striatal NPC line ST14A undergoes large changes during the differentiation process, and that these are strongly modulated by overexpression of the GDNF gene.

the GDNF over‐expression in differentiating ST-14A progenitor cells leads to an altered protein expression pattern, which is characterized by a strong increase of protein expression of ANXA5, GLU2B, PEBP1, MLRA, NACA, EF2, PRDX1 and a decrease of PCNA.
we have identified and verified a set of proteins whose expression is regulated by GDNFF overexpression in ST14A cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a proteome reference map for the differentiation of rat striatal progenitors.
the identification and characterization of the proteome of a rat progenitor cell line and its modulation by a neurotrophic factor.
the identification of proteins that might be involved in the differentiation processes of NPCs and the regulation of this process by GDNF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GDNF‐mediated changes of the proteome of ST14A cells during differentiation reflect a shift towards a neuronal phenotype.

GDNF overproduction in NPCs leads to a significant increase of the expression level of proteins involved in the regulation of cell proliferation, cell cycle, cell death and differentiation, as well as the expression level of several proteins involved in the maintenance of the cytoskeleton.
the differentiation‐related proteome of ST14A cells is strongly influenced by GDNF‐overexpression and that this influence can be detected in the proteome of the cells at all time‐points investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

2‐DE proteome profiling can be used to identify and characterize differentiation‐related protein expression changes in NPCs and that this approach can be extended by overexpression of neurotrophic factors to identify proteins that might be involved in the differentiation process.
the 2‐D proteomics approach is a powerful tool for identification of proteins and for analysis of their expression changes.

the GDNF‐induced differentiation of NPCs is associated with an increased expression of proteins involved in cell proliferation and cell cycle regulation, while proteins associated with the cytoskeletal system and cell adhesion are decreased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteome‐profiling approach is a powerful tool to investigate the differentiation process of progenitor cells.
proteome profiling can be used to study differentiation of NPCs and to detect the effects of neurotrophic factors on the differentiation process.
proteomics is a useful tool for studying differentiation and neurotrophic factor‐mediated signalling in neural progenitor cells.
